Resolves #18518

The grid witnesses now await the committed Workspace projection after observing the changed split, including instant FLIP landings whose worker-side motion class need not reach the DOM. They reject captured handled-projection failures before checking the rendered result. The unused pulse observers are removed: 55 net lines leave the two specs.

Evidence: L3 (headed Chrome, explicit Brain runtime, complete selected E2E files) → L3 required. No residual acceptance criteria; no whole-film, native matrix or new animation claim.

Change class: zero-delta. This changes test synchronization, with no production code or API change.

Micro-review eligible: test-only use of the existing projection promise and captured logs.

## AC Evidence

| Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | Three direct root-pulse barriers replaced by `refreshPromise.then` after the observed commit; their observer state/helpers removed. |
| AC-2 | AST/token comparison: the other 79 expect expressions are identical, including the deterministic transformed-geometry control. Input paths, ten feed cycles, scale-record mutation, both-direction geometry and residue checks remain. |
| AC-3 | The linked ten-cycle trace records a fresh post-gesture refresh settlement each time. A negative runtime control invokes the actual handled-failure producer and fails the new captured-warning assertion on cycle 1. |
| AC-4 | Both complete files run headed with the custom E2E config and explicit Brain checkout; baseline 3 failed/1 passed, candidate 4 passed. |

No production changes. A typed projection failure may resolve its attempt while replacing the retry promise, so the test also checks the existing captured warning. `agent-preflight` is not hosted here (npm Missing script); shared baseline jobs remain the hosted check authority.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**It declined the shortcut, and that is the most important thing in the diff.**

The tempting repair was `subtree: true` on the existing observer — the specs would have gone green immediately. They would have been observing the **header toolbar's overflow pulse**, a different producer, and one your own timings show is out of phase with the resize: a pulse **91 ms before** refresh entry and the last clear **299 ms before** settlement. Green for the wrong reason, asserting settlement while the projection is still in flight.

This PR removes the witness instead and awaits the owner. The comment says exactly that — *"Residue gates follow the completed projection, not an unrelated header pulse."*

**Verified the new barrier actually blocks**, because a barrier that returns immediately degrades the spec to a fixed-delay test without looking like one:

```
InstanceService.mjs:1188   const result = await scope[methodName].call(scope, ...args);
```

`callMethod` awaits the returned value, and `refreshPromise.then` with no arguments returns a promise settling with `refreshPromise`. So the RPC round-trip genuinely waits. It works, and it works for a non-obvious reason.

**Findings — one, non-blocking:**

`refreshPromise` is `{Promise|null}` (`Workspace.mjs:430`) and is **reassigned**, not just settled: chained at `:1710`, replaced at `:2393` and `:2754`, nulled at `:1271`. The spec resolves one snapshot and awaits that generation, so a refresh chained after the snapshot can still be running when the await returns.

**There is an existing, generation-safe idiom for this**, and it has precedent: `DockLockActionNL.spec.mjs:44` uses a settle-probe **counter** —

```js
await app.setProperties(WORKSPACE_ID, {settleProbeCount: value});
await expect.poll(… settledProbeCount).toBe(value)
```

a round-trip token, which cannot return on an earlier generation. `callMethod(…, 'refreshPromise.then')` has **zero occurrences** in the test tree before this PR.

Why it is non-blocking: the await here is a **barrier**, and every assertion after it is an `expect.poll`. An early return degrades to the previous polling behaviour rather than to a false pass, and the null case throws a TypeError — loud, not silent. So the failure modes are safe; the idiom is simply weaker than the one already in the tree.
